title: Persuading
job: Make a case, concede a point, hold your ground
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: -janayo PRESUPPOSES AGREEMENT. It is not an intensifier: it tells the listener they already know this. That is exactly why it persuades, and exactly why it is wrong with a stranger or an elder, who has agreed to nothing.
ENGLISH IS IT NOT? INVITES AN ANSWER AND -janayo DOES NOT. A tag question hands the floor over; -janayo closes the point, so a sentence ending in it can never be a genuine question.
V-gineun hajiman CONCEDES THE VERB BEFORE IT TURNS. The stem is nominalised with -gi, marked with -neun, granted, and then overturned: bissagineun hajiman joayo, it IS expensive, but it is good.
WRITE THE CONCESSIVE IN FULL. bissagineun, never bissagin: the contracted form collides with L2-M2's gin, long, and the full spelling is what keeps the two apart on the page.

mullon ... geuraedo ... IS A TURN, NOT A SENTENCE. mullon grants the other side a whole clause and geuraedo takes the ground back in the next one. Neither word does anything on its own, and the order is fixed.

KOREAN ARGUES BY CONCEDING FIRST AND ENGLISH BY STACKING CLAIMS. Transfer English directness and the turn reads as an attack; overcorrect and no position is left in it. After three levels of politeness the second failure is the commoner one.
sasil INTRODUCES THE FACT THE OTHER PERSON HAS NOT WEIGHED. It is not a softener and not a correction opener; it puts new evidence on the table, and the clause after it is that evidence.

NO LET US HERE. -(eu)psida is L4-M7's and it lifts the register besides. This module argues in one turn of ordinary conversation: the structured case is L5-M6's, irony is L5's, and declining is L4-M5's.

sentences.cue: We do have time now, you know. Let us go slowly.

words.note: isseoyo with -janayo on the stem. It does not ask and it does not insist; it says the listener already knows this, which is why it only works with someone who does.

sentences.trap: -janayo can only be said to someone who has already agreed. To a stranger it claims an agreement that was never given, and it lands as presumption.
sentences.sound: JI-geum SI-ga-ni IT-ja-na-yo. cheon-CHEON-hi GA-yo. The t of it- tenses the j after it, close to it-tja.

variations.cue: We do have time now, you know. Try it slowly.
variations.changed: the second half turned into an instruction

variations.cue: We do have time tomorrow, you know. Let us go slowly.
variations.changed: the shared fact moved to tomorrow

mistake.why: -janayo cannot ask. It tells the listener they already agree, so a question mark on it contradicts the ending: the question is sigan-i isseoyo?

sentences.usage: Talking a rushed friend out of hurrying.

sentences.cue: This restaurant is good, you know. Let us eat here.

words.note: joayo with -janayo. The h of the stem fuses with the j and this course writes what is said, as it writes jochi: jochanayo, never jotjanayo.

sentences.trap: The aspiration is written, not implied. jochanayo is the spelling this course uses everywhere the h of joh- meets a consonant.
sentences.sound: i-SIK-dang-i JO-cha-na-yo. yeo-GI-e-seo MEO-geo-yo. The cha is a clear aspirated ch, not a j.

variations.script: 이 식당이 좋잖아요. 여기에서 밥을 먹어요.
variations.cue: This restaurant is good, you know. Let us eat here.
variations.changed: the meal named

variations.script: 이 식당이 좋잖아요. 여기에서 같이 먹어요.
variations.cue: This restaurant is good, you know. Let us eat here together.
variations.changed: gachi added to the proposal

mistake.why: -janayo goes on the bare stem, not on a finished -ayo form. joh- plus the ending gives jochanayo.

sentences.usage: Settling where to eat with a colleague you know well.
sentences.mnemonic: h meets j and comes out ch.

sentences.cue: It is expensive, yes, but this one is really good.

words.note: bissayo nominalised with -gi and marked with -neun, ready to be conceded. Written in full, never as bissagin: the short form collides with L2-M2's gin, long.

sentences.trap: The concession is real, not rhetorical. bissagineun hajiman grants the price outright, and a turn that grants nothing before it turns reads as an attack.
sentences.sound: bi-SSA-gi-neun HA-ji-man, i-GEO-ga JEONG-mal JO-a-yo. The comma is a real pause after hajiman.

variations.cue: It is expensive, yes, but this one is better.
variations.changed: a comparison rather than a flat verdict

variations.cue: It is far, yes, but this one is really good.
variations.changed: distance conceded instead of price

mistake.why: bissagin is what speech does with it. This course writes the concessive in full, bissagineun, so that the -gi carrying the concession stays visible.

sentences.usage: Defending a purchase to someone who has just seen the price.

sentences.cue: It is far, yes, but there are buses often.

words.note: The same concessive on meoreoyo. The l of the stem comes back in front of -gi, so it is meolgineun and never meoreogineun.

sentences.trap: meoreoyo hides its l and -gineun brings it back. The stem is meol-, and every ending that starts with a consonant sees it.
sentences.sound: MEOL-gi-neun HA-ji-man, BEO-seu-ga JA-ju I-sseo-yo. meol is one beat with a clear l.

variations.cue: It is far, yes, but the bus comes often.
variations.changed: the bus arriving rather than existing

variations.cue: It is expensive, yes, but there are buses often.
variations.changed: price conceded instead of distance

mistake.why: hajiman belongs to the conceded half and cannot be cut away from it. The comma goes after hajiman, not before it.

sentences.usage: Arguing for a flat that is out of the centre.

sentences.display: Mullon jom bissayo. Geuraedo i-geo-ga deo joayo.
sentences.script: 물론 좀 비싸요. 그래도 이거가 더 좋아요.
sentences.cue: Of course it is a bit expensive. Even so, this one is better.
sentences.literal: of-course a-bit expensive. even-so this-thing-SUBJ more good

words.note: It grants the other side a whole clause and then stops. It never appears without a geuraedo clause after it, and standing alone it sounds like plain agreement.
The half of the turn that takes the ground back. It heads its own sentence, after the full stop that ends mullon's, and it is what makes the concession a move.

sentences.trap: Two sentences, in that order. Reversed, the turn concedes the very point it was trying to make, and a listener hears agreement.
sentences.sound: MUL-lon JOM bi-SSA-yo. geu-RAE-do i-GEO-ga DEO JO-a-yo. The ll of mullon is held.

variations.display: Mullon jom meoreoyo. Geuraedo i-geo-ga deo joayo.
variations.script: 물론 좀 멀어요. 그래도 이거가 더 좋아요.
variations.cue: Of course it is a bit far. Even so, this one is better.
variations.changed: distance conceded instead of price

variations.display: Mullon jom bissayo. Geuraedo jeongmal joayo.
variations.script: 물론 좀 비싸요. 그래도 정말 좋아요.
variations.cue: Of course it is a bit expensive. Even so, it is really good.
variations.changed: the second half shortened to the verdict

mistake.display: Geuraedo jom bissayo. Mullon i-geo-ga deo joayo.
mistake.script: 그래도 좀 비싸요. 물론 이거가 더 좋아요.
mistake.why: The order is fixed: mullon grants first, geuraedo takes the ground back second. Reversed, the turn ends by conceding.

sentences.usage: Making the case for the pricier option in a shop.

sentences.cue: I do do it, but it did not go well.

words.note: haeyo under the concessive. It concedes the action itself, so hagineun hajiman is I did do it, but — and the but is where the position comes back.

sentences.trap: hagineun concedes the doing, not the result. It is how you keep credit for the effort while admitting the outcome.
sentences.sound: HA-gi-neun HA-ji-man, JAL AN DWAE-sseo-yo. an leans into dwaesseoyo as one breath.

variations.cue: I do do it, but I am not really sure.
variations.changed: the second half hedged rather than negative

variations.cue: I do do it, but there is not much time.
variations.changed: a different reason after the turn

mistake.why: hagin is the spoken contraction. This course writes hagineun in full so the -gi that carries the concession stays on the page.

sentences.usage: Reporting on a task that half worked.
sentences.mnemonic: Concede the doing, keep the point.

sentences.display: Jigeum an bappeunikka hwaksilhi hal su isseoyo.
sentences.script: 지금 안 바쁘니까 확실히 할 수 있어요.
sentences.cue: Since I am not busy now, I can certainly do it.
sentences.literal: now not busy-since certainly do-ing way exists

words.note: The adverb that puts weight behind a claim, sitting in front of the verb. It states confidence rather than raising the voice, which is what an argument in this register needs.

sentences.trap: hwaksilhi commits the speaker. It is not jeongmal, which colours the claim; it says the speaker will answer for it.
sentences.sound: JI-geum AN ba-PPEU-ni-kka hwak-SIL-hi HAL SU I-sseo-yo. hwaksilhi tenses its s, close to hwak-ssil-hi.

variations.display: Jigeum an bappeunikka hwaksilhi gal su isseoyo.
variations.script: 지금 안 바쁘니까 확실히 갈 수 있어요.
variations.cue: Since I am not busy now, I can certainly go.
variations.changed: going rather than doing

variations.cue: Since there is no time, I certainly cannot do it.
variations.changed: the same confidence behind a refusal

mistake.display: Jigeum an bappeunikka hwaksilhi hal isseoyo.
mistake.script: 지금 안 바쁘니까 확실히 할 있어요.
mistake.why: su is not optional. L2-M1's ability frame is V-(eu)l su isseoyo in three pieces, and without the bound noun there is no ability in the sentence.

sentences.usage: Volunteering for a job in front of the team.
sentences.mnemonic: hwaksilhi puts your name on it.

sentences.cue: Actually, there is a reason for this.

words.note: It introduces the fact the other person has not weighed. Not a softener and not a correction opener: the clause after it is the evidence.
The noun for a reason you can give. L4-M2's ttaemune states a cause inside a sentence; iyu is the thing itself, and it takes the ordinary particles.

sentences.trap: sasil is not English actually as a polite correction. It promises evidence, so the sentence after it has to supply some.
sentences.sound: SA-sil i-GEO-neun I-yu-ga I-sseo-yo. sasil has two even beats and no stress of its own.

variations.cue: Actually, there is no reason for this.
variations.changed: the fact turned negative

variations.cue: Actually, I do not know the reason.
variations.changed: iyu as the object rather than the subject

mistake.why: geunde only changes direction. sasil puts on the table a fact the other person has not weighed, and that is what this turn needs.

sentences.usage: Bringing new information into a disagreement at work.

sentences.cue: Of course it is good, you know. Even so, it is a bit expensive.

words.note: The -janayo of this module on bissayo. In the geuraedo half it is what holds the position: the price is something the listener already knows.

sentences.trap: Both halves lean on shared knowledge, so the turn only works between people who share it. Said to a stranger, it claims a history that is not there.
sentences.sound: MUL-lon JO-cha-na-yo. geu-RAE-do JOM bi-SSA-ja-na-yo. Both -janayo endings fall at the end.

variations.cue: Of course it is good, you know. Even so, it is a bit far.
variations.changed: a plain statement in the second half

variations.cue: Of course it is good, you know. Even so, it really is expensive.
variations.changed: jeongmal instead of jom, which hardens it

mistake.why: hajiman joins two halves of one sentence. mullon's partner across a full stop is geuraedo, and only geuraedo carries the even so this turn needs.

sentences.usage: Holding out against a friend's recommendation.

sentences.display: Naeil-eun an bappeujanayo. Geureomyeon gachi gal su isseoyo.
sentences.script: 내일은 안 바쁘잖아요. 그러면 같이 갈 수 있어요.
sentences.cue: You are not busy tomorrow, you know. Then we can go together.
sentences.literal: tomorrow-TOP not busy-you-know. then together go-ing way exists

words.note: -janayo on bappayo, whose stem is bappeu-, so the ending goes straight onto it. With an in front it says the opposite, and both presuppose agreement.

sentences.trap: This turn tells the listener something about their own diary. It only works if they really did say so, which is the whole condition on -janayo.
sentences.sound: NAE-i-reun AN ba-PPEU-ja-na-yo. geu-REO-myeon GA-chi GAL SU I-sseo-yo.

variations.display: Naeil-eun an bappeujanayo. Geureomyeon gachi hal su isseoyo.
variations.script: 내일은 안 바쁘잖아요. 그러면 같이 할 수 있어요.

variations.changed: doing rather than going

variations.display: Jigeum an bappeujanayo. Geureomyeon gachi gal su isseoyo.
variations.script: 지금 안 바쁘잖아요. 그러면 같이 갈 수 있어요.
variations.cue: You are not busy now, you know. Then we can go together.

mistake.display: Naeil-eun an bappeujanayo. Geureomyeon gachi gapsida.
mistake.script: 내일은 안 바쁘잖아요. 그러면 같이 갑시다.
mistake.why: -(eu)psida is L4-M7's and it lifts the register in the middle of an ordinary turn. gachi gal su isseoyo keeps the whole turn at one level.
